title: Mandibular intraosseous lesion
html: A 48-year-old woman came to the Oral Diagnostic Center, University of São Paulo, São Paulo, Brazil, for oral diagnosis and evaluation of an asymptomatic bone defect in the left mandibular arch, incidentally detected during imaging performed for rehabilitation planning. The patient had a history of systemic arterial hypertension controlled with diuretic medication and angiotensin II receptor antagonists and reported no history of smoking or alcohol consumption. Intraoral examination was noncontributory, as no significant bone expansion was observed and the overlying mucosa appeared normal.
